title: Englewood
name: Englewood
metaDescription: Englewood 1031 exchange guidance for CityCenter mixed-use retail, Swedish Medical Center-area office, and Santa Fe corridor property south of Denver.

sections.html: Englewood is a small, inner-ring suburb wedged between Denver and Littleton, and its commercial story runs through one redevelopment site more than anywhere else in the south metro. What used to be Cinderella City, once one of the largest enclosed malls in the country, is now CityCenter Englewood, and that single site shapes how the rest of the submarket gets read.

sections.heading: CityCenter Sits on a Landmark Site
sections.html:
Cinderella City opened in the 1960s and grew into a massive regional mall before closing and getting demolished in the late 1990s. CityCenter Englewood replaced it with a mixed-use development centered on a light rail station, city offices, retail, and multifamily housing. It's a very different kind of asset than the strip retail along Broadway just a few blocks away, and buyers should not assume the two comp against each other just because they share a zip code.

The light rail line that runs through CityCenter dates back to the system's original southwest extension in the early 2000s, and it was a real driver of the redevelopment decision to begin with. A buyer should know that CityCenter's transit-oriented design took its shape from that station rather than adding transit access later, which explains why the site's density and mix look different from an older, car-oriented shopping center nearby.

sections.heading: The Property Types Here
sections.html:
What actually shows up for sale in Englewood:

  • mixed-use retail and multifamily near CityCenter and the light rail station
  • medical office near Swedish Medical Center
  • older strip retail and commercial buildings along Broadway
  • light industrial and flex space along the Santa Fe Drive corridor shared with Littleton

sections.heading: A Hospital and a Former Corporate Campus
sections.html:
Swedish Medical Center anchors a real medical office cluster on the west side of Englewood, and that demand has stayed steady regardless of what's happening with retail vacancy elsewhere in the city. On the other side of town, the large corporate campus once occupied by a national satellite TV company has gone through its own repositioning as that tenant scaled back, and buildings like it are a reminder that a single-tenant corporate campus carries real concentration risk when that one tenant's business changes.

Old Hampden Avenue, a stretch of smaller retail predating both CityCenter and the corporate campus era, still carries some of Englewood's original mid-century commercial buildings. It's a different tier of property entirely, smaller floor plates, older mechanical systems, and a buyer should underwrite it as its own niche rather than expecting CityCenter-level rents on a building three decades older. A lender comparing the two corridors will typically apply a wider spread to a Broadway-area deal than a CityCenter one, reflecting that difference in building age and tenant credit quality.

sections.heading: Diligence That Matters in Englewood
sections.html: Confirm which micro-market a parcel sits in, CityCenter, Swedish Medical Center, Broadway, or Santa Fe, before comping it citywide. On any single-tenant former corporate campus building, model out the real cost of re-tenanting to multiple smaller users if the original tenant continues downsizing, rather than assuming a like-for-like backfill.

sections.heading: Positioning an Englewood Identification
sections.html: Medical office near Swedish Medical Center is generally the most stable single asset in this submarket and often gets identified alongside a Littleton or Highlands Ranch property for geographic and asset-class balance. CityCenter retail pairs well with a Lakewood Belmar asset given the similar mall-to-mixed-use redevelopment story behind both. A qualified intermediary should confirm any city redevelopment agreement or public financing district tied to a CityCenter parcel, since public-private redevelopment deals like this one sometimes carry ongoing tax increment obligations that a buyer needs to underwrite into net operating income. A rent roll for any CityCenter parcel should also separate the retail component from the residential component if a building has both, since those two income streams carry different lease terms, turnover patterns, and renewal assumptions. A replacement property identification for Englewood should note the exact corridor by name in the paperwork, rather than only the city, since CityCenter, the Swedish Medical Center cluster, and Broadway strip retail all underwrite as separate micro-markets rather than one blended average. A tax advisor coordinating Form 8824 for an Englewood exchange should keep those three asset classes clearly separated on the return, since depreciation schedules and cost segregation treatment differ across mixed-use retail, medical office, and older strip commercial. Confirm this breakdown with a qualified intermediary before the 45-day window closes rather than sorting it out afterward.

faqs.q: What replaced Cinderella City in Englewood?
faqs.a: CityCenter Englewood, a mixed-use development with retail, city offices, multifamily housing, and a light rail station, built after the original mall was demolished in the late 1990s.

faqs.q: Is medical office near Swedish Medical Center a stable 1031 replacement?
faqs.a: Generally yes. That demand has held steady independent of retail vacancy trends elsewhere in Englewood.

faqs.q: What's the risk with a single-tenant former corporate campus building?
faqs.a: Concentration risk. If the original anchor tenant continues downsizing, model the real cost of re-tenanting to multiple smaller users rather than assuming a like-for-like backfill.

faqs.q: Should Broadway strip retail be comped against CityCenter?
faqs.a: No, they're different formats and different tenant profiles even though they sit close together. Comp each against its own asset class.

faqs.q: What does an Englewood identification usually pair with?
faqs.a: Medical office near Swedish Medical Center often pairs with a Littleton or Highlands Ranch asset, while CityCenter retail pairs well with a Lakewood Belmar property given their similar redevelopment history.
